claims.text: Net profit rose about 6% to ₹82 crore.
Operating margins contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2%.
Copper, the company's main raw material, rose nearly 14% during the quarter.
Shares of the company fell 3.2% to ₹1,012 on the NSE on Friday after the results.
For the full year FY27 we are maintaining our revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent.
Bharuch will contribute from the second half.
Data-centre cables are now about 9 percent of our domestic revenue, and we think that can double in two years.
About two-thirds of our contracts have price-variation clauses, but they reset with a lag of one to two quarters.
Receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year.
Bharuch capex is ₹620 crore in total, about 70 percent already spent.
Capex is funded mainly through internal accruals and some term debt.
Net debt to equity is 0.35 times.
Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors.
Revenue from operations was ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27, up 18.0% YoY.
EBITDA was ₹140 crore in Q1 FY27, up 2.6% YoY.
EBITDA margin was 11.2% in Q1 FY27, down 170 bps YoY.
Profit after tax was ₹82 crore in Q1 FY27, up 5.9% YoY.
Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.
Exports contributed 21% of revenue (Q1 FY26: 16%).
The new Bharuch (Gujarat) plant adds about 30% to cable capacity and is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27.
We expect to pass on the sharp rise in copper prices to customers over the next two quarters.
The company received a GST demand order of ₹46.3 crore (including interest and penalty) relating to input tax credit claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.
The company believes it has a strong case on merits and does not expect any material impact on its financial position or operations.
Promoters & promoter group holding was 58.2% in Jun 2026, 58.2% in Mar 2026, and 58.4% in Jun 2025.
Of promoter holding, pledged percentage was 4.1% in Jun 2026, 6.0% in Mar 2026, and 11.5% in Jun 2025.
Foreign institutional investors (FII) holding was 11.8% in Jun 2026, 10.9% in Mar 2026, and 9.2% in Jun 2025.
Domestic institutional investors (DII) holding was 14.6% in Jun 2026, 14.1% in Mar 2026, and 12.7% in Jun 2025.
Public and others holding was 15.4% in Jun 2026, 16.8% in Mar 2026, and 19.7% in Jun 2025.
Margins are down 170 basis points, as noted by the analyst.
EBITDA margin was 12.9% in Q1 FY26, according to the consolidated highlights.
